_comment: The ONE place the homepage figures are set. scripts/check-metrics.mjs fails the build if index.html disagrees with this file, so a number cannot drift in the page without drifting here first. Update this, run `npm run metrics:check`, then edit the page.
measuredAgainst: CAIRN Trust Fabric 2.10.16, extracted from the published .deb, on the same host and Node as every earlier run in this series. 2.10.16 changed nothing the gate runs; re-taken because the headline names the release. Taken under light load, with 2.10.16 and 2.10.15 run in turn, three times each, in the same session.
source: docs/CLAIMS.md and the pillar list in the CAIRN source repository

governedPillars.label: governed pillars
governedPillars.basis: PATH, CAIRN, COMPASS, ATLAS, FORGE, CRUCIBLE, BEACON

deployment.label: deployment
deployment.basis: no CAIRN-operated server is involved in a customer deployment

gateCost.label: per decision that runs no code
gateCost.basis: p50, taken 2026-09-30 against the SHIPPED 2.10.16 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 05e7e91bc5b68ff8daac7a10cb596afff78fbd4641c4c6df3482d228d34ef83d), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up, on the development host, not in the Windows Sandbox used to walk the installer (no internet, no GPU, not representative). The host was under LIGHT LOAD, not idle: CPU 3 to 12 per cent. Three runs each, interleaved 2.10.16, 2.10.15. p50 by scenario, runs a / b / c: read 0.226 / 0.226 / 0.221, denied 0.228 / 0.235 / 0.230, write 0.260 / 0.254 / 0.259, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.285 / 0.293 / 0.277. 2.10.15 in the same session: read 0.224 / 0.227 / 0.225, denied 0.228 / 0.225 / 0.230, write 0.260 / 0.254 / 0.256, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.289 / 0.285 / 0.290. Every difference is inside 2.10.15's own spread: level. p99 is about 2.2 to 2.4 ms, because a ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 346 ms and is NOT included in this figure.

_removed.automatedTests: Removed 2026-09-06. The page carried '2,856 automated tests' under a heading reading 'Live Telemetry' while the real figure was 3,303 — a number that had drifted by 447 and was never live. It is also the one figure CAIRN's own register discipline forbids as a headline: a test count is a measurement, never readiness. If a volume figure is wanted here, it must be one that does not rot and does not invite that reading.
_removed.trackedClaims: Removed 2026-09-06 with register.html. The strip read '143 claims in the public register' and there is no public register any more, so the figure described a surface a reader cannot reach. A number that is accurate about an internal document and false about this site is the defect this file exists to prevent.
_removed.claimsBreakdown: Removed 2026-09-06 with the homepage register extract: Works 92, Partial 37, Never 5, Roadmap 9. Kept here so a later session can see what the figures were rather than recounting.
_removed.gateCost_0_20_0_26: Replaced 2026-09-16. "0.20–0.26 ms to evaluate a policy decision", basis "measured against CAIRN Trust Fabric 2.10.1". It was measured on 2026-08-22 against earlier code, and re-taking it against the published 2.10.1 found writes at ~1.9 ms. It also said "a policy decision" of a gate whose decisions that run code cost three orders of magnitude more — the exact single-number mistake docs/GATE-PERFORMANCE.md was written to prevent.
_removed.gateCost_0_2_2_2: Replaced 2026-09-18, when the fix it named shipped. "0.2–2.2 ms", basis the SHIPPED 2.10.1. That figure was correct and is now historical: the page-cache fix it described as "becomes the figure when that ships" shipped in 2.10.2, and re-taking the measurement against the published 2.10.2 .deb on the same host found writes at 0.258 ms rather than 1.870. The sawtooth across each checkpoint cycle is gone at p50. Raw for both runs is in validation/results/ in the distribution repository.
_removed.gateCost_0_20_0_26_on_2_10_7: Replaced 2026-09-21 when 2.10.8 shipped. "0.20–0.26 ms", basis: p50, re-taken 2026-09-21 against the SHIPPED 2.10.7 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 235f82bc958e312b48dc540de14f14e3c36ce78e169481257b7003526edd9766), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). Same host and Node as the 2.10.1 and 2.10.2 runs, so all three compare: i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up, machine otherwise idle. p50 by scenario: read 0.201, denied 0.204, write 0.236, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.262. These sit about 10 per cent below the 2.10.2 column and that is NOT claimed as an improvement: the gap is within what host state explains, and nothing in 2.10.7 targets gate cost. What the re-take establishes is that the gate-path change in 7d2440f did not regress it. p99 reaches ~2.1-2.4 ms, because a ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere; the headline is a p50 and says so. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs ~313 ms and is NOT included in this figure. Quoting one number for both is the mistake docs/GATE-PERFORMANCE.md exists to prevent.
_removed.gateCost_0_22_0_28_on_2_10_8_under_load: Replaced 2026-09-28 when 2.10.9 shipped, by the same value re-measured on 2.10.9 on an idle machine. Basis as it stood: p50, taken 2026-09-21 against the SHIPPED 2.10.8 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 c0efa2e809af10ff2694370353e5d35212a0e1f139bfc1c43efefded43bb1416), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up. The machine was NOT idle: two other development sessions were running tests. p50 by scenario: read 0.223, denied 0.219, write 0.255, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.277. 2.10.7 re-taken immediately before under the same load: read 0.235, denied 0.251, write 0.262, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.317, so 2.10.8 is no slower in any scenario and the gate-path change did not regress it. The range is higher than the idle 2.10.7 figure (0.20 to 0.26) because of load, not because of the release; the headline uses the number measured on this release rather than borrowing an idle one from the last. p99 under load reached about 3.2 to 3.5 ms. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 325 ms and is NOT included in this figure.
_removed.gateCost_0_22_0_28_on_2_10_9_idle: Replaced 2026-09-28 when 2.10.10 shipped, by the same value re-measured on 2.10.10. Basis as it stood: p50, taken 2026-09-28 against the SHIPPED 2.10.9 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 d2137717698d9fe9197c89713b0ad4009e4eba1dcd3d66a1ccb44e470b486273), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up. The machine was idle: CPU averaged 3.4 per cent over ten seconds before the runs. p50 by scenario: read 0.222, denied 0.224, write 0.241, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.276. 2.10.8 re-taken immediately after on the same idle machine: read 0.222, denied 0.230, write 0.256, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.274, so 2.10.9 is no slower in any scenario. Re-taken rather than carried forward because 2.10.9 changed a module the gate imports (the memory search). The idle 2.10.8 re-take matched its earlier under-load p50 within a few per cent; the load showed at p99, which is about 2.2 to 2.3 ms idle on 2.10.9 against 3.2 to 3.5 ms under load on 2.10.8. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 336 ms and is NOT included in this figure.
_removed.gateCost_0_22_0_28_on_2_10_10_idle: Replaced 2026-09-28 when 2.10.11 shipped, because 2.10.11 is slower: it added a self-protection check to every decision, and the re-measurement moved the range to 0.24–0.30 ms. Value as it stood: "0.22–0.28 ms". Basis as it stood: p50, taken 2026-09-28 against the SHIPPED 2.10.10 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 d4fb408afff8c90fc2644c0671711da30888bd104fd6d3ca4a59334f3629e8c6), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up. The machine was idle: CPU averaged 3.5 per cent over ten seconds before the runs. p50 by scenario: read 0.218, denied 0.228, write 0.246, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.276. 2.10.9 re-taken in the same session: read 0.216, denied 0.225, write 0.243, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.273, within about one per cent in every scenario. 2.10.10 changed nothing the gate imports apart from the version stamp; re-taken rather than carried forward because the headline names the release. p99 is about 2.2 to 2.7 ms, because a ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 335 ms and is NOT included in this figure.
_removed.gateCost_0_24_0_30_on_2_10_11: Replaced 2026-09-29 when 2.10.12 shipped and recovered most of 2.10.11's cost. Value as it stood: "0.24–0.30 ms". Basis as it stood: p50, taken 2026-09-28 against the SHIPPED 2.10.11 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 fb0bb2917fd86bd21ba66843209238fb891c0e9e58574aceb2a5428c645b011f), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up. The machine was idle: CPU averaged 5.5 per cent over ten seconds before the runs. p50 by scenario: read 0.249, denied 0.244, write 0.270, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.299. 2.10.10 re-taken in the same session: read 0.217, denied 0.218, write 0.248, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.279, reproducing its earlier figures, so the difference is the release. 2.10.11 is about 0.02 to 0.03 ms (7 to 15 per cent) slower per decision because of a security check added to every decision; making it cheaper is follow-up work. p99 is about 2.2 to 2.4 ms, because a ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 343 ms and is NOT included in this figure.
_removed.gateCost_0_23_0_28_on_2_10_12: Replaced 2026-09-29 when 2.10.13 shipped and recovered the rest of 2.10.11's cost. Value as it stood: "0.23–0.28 ms". Basis as it stood: p50, taken 2026-09-29 against the SHIPPED 2.10.12 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 b4d48c58fb800085f2ca9cdbfeeb4fd3c0b055d5f4113af24b61138d52de688e), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up. The machine was idle: CPU averaged 3.3 per cent over ten seconds before the runs. p50 by scenario: read 0.230, denied 0.229, write 0.258, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.276. In the same session 2.10.10 measured read 0.218, denied 0.226, write 0.246, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.275, and 2.10.11 read 0.245, denied 0.242, write 0.271, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.301. So 2.10.12 is 5 to 8 per cent faster than 2.10.11 and has recovered MOST, not all, of the cost 2.10.11 added: level with 2.10.10 for already-CRITICAL and denied, about 0.012 ms slower for read and write. p99 is about 2.2 to 2.4 ms, because a ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 339 ms and is NOT included in this figure.
_removed.gateCost_basis_on_2_10_13: Basis replaced 2026-09-29 when 2.10.14 shipped; the value did not change. Basis as it stood: p50, taken 2026-09-29 against the SHIPPED 2.10.13 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 e79644bbdbc25f76d6c870e6b5b961cc428e2c67ce24d3db5ca911123564feea), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up. The machine was idle: CPU 0 to 4 per cent, Docker stopped, an idle Windows Sandbox memory process still resident. Two runs each, interleaved 2.10.13, 2.10.10, 2.10.12. p50 by scenario, run a / run b: read 0.222 / 0.222, denied 0.239 / 0.235, write 0.249 / 0.251, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.281 / 0.280. 2.10.10 in the same session: read 0.214 / 0.221, denied 0.224 / 0.237, write 0.248 / 0.254, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.271 / 0.281. Every difference between 2.10.13 and 2.10.10 is smaller than the difference between 2.10.10's own two runs: level within the variation, not faster. p99 is about 2.2 to 2.4 ms, because a ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 345 ms and is NOT included in this figure.
_removed.gateCost_0_22_0_28_on_2_10_14: Replaced 2026-09-30 when 2.10.15 shipped. Basis as it stood: p50, taken 2026-09-29 against the SHIPPED 2.10.14 extracted from the published .deb (sha256 1d69945867cc68482a3bfccd4f9f4c3bb5c880fb1a8569dd043c2bb79b703471), with the published method in the distribution repository (validation/). i9-12900K, 24 logical cores, Windows 11, Node 24.2.0, 500 iterations after 20 warm-up, on the development host, not in the Windows Sandbox used to walk the installer (no internet, no GPU, not representative). The host was under LIGHT LOAD, not idle: CPU 5 to 11 per cent with one spike. Three runs each, interleaved 2.10.14, 2.10.13. p50 by scenario, runs a / b / c: read 0.218 / 0.221 / 0.221, denied 0.224 / 0.227 / 0.225, write 0.250 / 0.256 / 0.250, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.274 / 0.278 / 0.279. 2.10.13 in the same session: read 0.226 / 0.218 / 0.224, denied 0.228 / 0.222 / 0.223, write 0.257 / 0.246 / 0.248, execute-already-CRITICAL 0.281 / 0.277 / 0.274. Every difference is inside 2.10.13's own spread: level, as identical gate code should be. p99 is about 2.2 to 2.4 ms, because a ledger checkpoint is real work that has to happen somewhere. A decision that parses a PowerShell script on Windows costs about 337 ms and is NOT included in this figure.
